headline: Spain's privacy regulator logged the first data breach an AI agent carried out on its own, hours before European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen asked the bloc to answer AI-powered hacking and sabotage as one.

emerging_trends.text: A Spanish regulator has now logged an intrusion that an AI agent ran end to end, Mandiant traced a hijacked coding assistant that seeded the Shai-Hulud worm through roughly 100 repositories, and von der Leyen asked frontier labs to slow self-improving models, which moves autonomous attack capability from demonstration into the incident-report column.

topics.title: Oracle Ships 800 Fixes as Google Patches an Exploited Pixel Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: CISA added two more exploited flaws on September 16, 2026—CVE-2026-76460, an incorrect use of privileged APIs in Cisco Identity Services Engine, and CVE-2026-87886 in the Acronis backup plugin—and warned the same day that attackers now exploit the critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect file transfer flaw that ConnectWise patched on September 14, 2026; CISA had already cataloged CVE-2026-58704, the 8.0-rated permission bypass in the Pixel cellular modem that attackers use in limited targeted attacks.
topics.summary: Oracle's September update closed more than 800 vulnerabilities across 17 product families, over 100 of them critical, and Google's September Pixel release carried 110 fixes. Update Pixel phones and self-hosted ScreenConnect servers first, review ScreenConnect session and file transfer logs for transfers no technician made, then schedule the Oracle work.

sources.title: Oracle Patches 800+ Vulnerabilities in September 2026 Security Update
Google fixes actively exploited Android zero-day on Pixel devices
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: Poisoned Plugins Backdoor WordPress and cPanel Hosts
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-87886 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 16, 2026, hours after Acronis confirmed that attackers use the 7.8-rated insecure file permissions flaw in its backup plugin for cPanel, WebHost Manager, and Plesk to raise a local Linux account to root in limited targeted attacks; SecurityWeek reported that unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in The Events Calendar expose more than 200,000 WordPress sites to takeover; Wordfence blocked thousands of attempts to upload PHP backdoors through WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture, a premium plugin running on more than 6,000 sites; and tampered Admin Menu Editor Pro updates, pushed after a threat actor compromised the maintainer's website, planted a hidden user account on 1,500 WordPress sites.
topics.summary: Hosting stacks run on third-party plugins that update themselves and that nobody audits. Patch the Acronis backup plugin, The Events Calendar, and WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture, then hunt for unfamiliar administrator accounts and new PHP files in upload directories.

sources.title: Unauthenticated RCE Flaws Could Expose 200,000+ WordPress Sites to Takeover

topics.title: Runaway Agents and AI-Found Bugs Swamp Defenders
topics.latest_developments: Forever Security showed that one ordinary browser extension seizes the AI assistants built into five Chromium products—Gemini Live in Chrome, Perplexity Comet, Microsoft Edge, Opera Neon, and the Claude in Chrome extension—with a single click after installation, and Dark Reading detailed BragJack, an attack that turns a browser's built-in assistant against its owner to reach sensitive information, run malicious actions, and exfiltrate data; Mandiant's AI Risk and Resilience report, built on its own casework and Google Threat Intelligence Group telemetry, tracked attacks moving from direct prompts to indirect prompt injection and AI supply chain compromise and cited one autonomous agent that ran up a $50,000 cloud bill; and Cisco Talos argued that AI keeps surfacing vulnerabilities nobody can patch, leaving network segmentation and next-generation firewall and intrusion prevention pairs as the compensating layer.
topics.summary: Enterprises now run agents that call APIs, change production configurations, and spend money without a human in the loop, and the browser assistant sitting on every employee laptop belongs on that list. Gate proposed agent actions before they touch production systems, cap cloud spending per agent, restrict extension installation, and segment what agents cannot patch.

sources.title: BragJack Attack Can Turn a Browser's Agentic AI Against It
One Extension Could Hijack AI Assistants Across Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon and Claude
One runaway AI agent racked up a $50,000 cloud bill
Securing the unpatchable in an age of AI-driven vulnerabilities

topics.title: Von der Leyen Asks Europe to Answer Sabotage Together
topics.latest_developments: Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, used her State of the Union address in Strasbourg on September 16, 2026 to call for a joint European response to cyberattacks and sabotage, pointing to recent incidents in Denmark, Lithuania, and Poland and an attempted drone attack in Leipzig; she warned that advanced AI could unleash hacking on an unprecedented scale, asked the leading AI labs to slow self-improving models and promised to invite them in, committed the bloc to work with Canada and the United Kingdom on evaluating and verifying advanced systems and on early warning, and outlined new protections for children against social media. In Washington the same day, House Energy and Commerce Chairman Brett Guthrie said the FRONTIER Act, the chamber's AI safety bill, will likely wait until 2027 because he declines to rush it through a lame duck session.
topics.summary: European Union governments have handled cyber and physical sabotage nationally, and von der Leyen wants the bloc to answer as one while Congress lets its own AI bill slip past this term. Companies selling connected products into Europe should watch for coordination duties stacked on top of the Cyber Resilience Act's 24-hour incident reporting clock.

sources.title: EU chief wants joint response to cyberattacks, sabotage
EU Chief Warns of AI-Powered Hacking, Moves to Rein In Social Media
Self-improving AI should slow down, von der Leyen tells EU lawmakers
Key lawmaker suggests action on AI safety legislation will wait until 2027

topics.title: Spain Reports the First Agentic AI Data Breach
topics.latest_developments: The Spanish Data Protection Agency received notification of an attack that an AI agent running on a known large language model carried out, chaining a successful login, vulnerability discovery, and access to personal data, which SecurityWeek calls the first agentic AI breach a regulator has logged; Mandiant separately traced an attacker who hijacked an active AI coding-assistant session at a software-as-a-service provider, steered the assistant into recommending poisoned software, and then watched the Shai-Hulud worm move across roughly 100 internal code repositories, taking repository secrets and source code.
topics.summary: One AI agent ran a full intrusion sequence against a Spanish organization, and a hijacked coding assistant seeded a worm inside a vendor's repositories. Treat agent sessions as privileged accounts: log every action they take, rotate repository secrets, and require human approval before an assistant installs a dependency.

sources.title: First Agentic AI Data Breach Reported to Spanish Regulator
Spain reports first alleged AI-powered data theft attack
Attacker Hijacks AI Coding Assistant Session, Spreads Shai-Hulud Across About 100 Repositories

topics.title: Forged Admin Tokens Open WSO2 API Manager
topics.latest_developments: watchTowr reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-5430, a 9.8-rated failure to verify a cryptographic signature in WSO2 API Manager that lets an attacker forge a JSON Web Token, authenticate as an administrator, and take over accounts, a flaw the Hacktron Team found and reported; attackers separately began exploiting CVE-2026-89026, rated 9.8, in the Issabel Framework, where a hard-coded credential lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run operating system commands on the open-source unified communications PBX.
topics.summary: WSO2 API Manager fronts enterprise APIs and the data behind them, and Issabel runs corporate phone systems, so both give an intruder administrative reach in one step. Apply the vendor fixes and audit logs for administrative sessions and commands that no legitimate login produced.

sources.title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
Enterprises Warned of Attacks Exploiting WSO2 Vulnerability
Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution

topics.title: Iran's CHOSEN BRICK Malware Spies on Dissidents
topics.latest_developments: The FBI, the United Kingdom's National Cyber Security Centre, and the Netherlands' AIVD named the malware on September 16, 2026: CHOSEN BRICK, which Iranian state operators have delivered through social messaging apps to dissidents, activists, and journalists in the three countries since at least 2025, and the FBI detailed how the operators run command and control through Telegram.
topics.summary: CHOSEN BRICK copies a target's email and chat messages, captures screenshots, and switches on the microphone of an infected Windows machine. People in exile communities, newsrooms, and human rights organizations should treat unsolicited files arriving over Telegram and WhatsApp as hostile and check devices against the agencies' published indicators.

sources.title: Iranian hackers use CHOSEN BRICK Windows malware to spy on targets
US, UK, Dutch Agencies Expose Iranian 'Chosen Brick' Surveillance Malware

topics.title: NightEagle Hits Russia as a North Korean Toolkit Lands in Seoul
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky widened the Russian picture on September 16, 2026, naming three clusters that hit enterprises there: NightEagle, also tracked as APT-Q-95 and active since at least 2023, which plants the GhostContainer backdoor, stages its tools on GitHub, and exploits weaknesses in Active Directory and Remote Desktop Protocol, alongside Hacking Cat and Toy Ghouls, which deliver backdoors, ransomware, and wipers; Dark Reading separately reported that a likely North Korean group used a previously undocumented Linux espionage toolkit to seize load balancers at South Korean media and automotive companies, read communications, and push deeper into those networks.
topics.summary: All four crews aim at infrastructure that security teams rarely instrument: domain controllers, remote access services, and the Linux appliances balancing traffic at the network edge. Hunt on those devices for unexpected tunnels, new local accounts, and outbound connections to GitHub-hosted payloads.

sources.title: NightEagle targets Russian companies
Three Threat Groups Target Russian Enterprises With Backdoors, Ransomware, and Wipers

topics.title: Hackers Dump a Flock Safety Camera's Software and Data
topics.latest_developments: A hacker collective pulled down a Flock Safety camera, extracted the software running inside it, and published the contents, and Wired counted thousands of videos and logs showing that the single device captured 1.6 million images of 50,000 vehicles in 21 days; The Record reported the same day that Washington, D.C.'s police department has used Flock camera data in misconduct investigations of its own officers, which drew a formal complaint from the officers' union.
topics.summary: Flock Safety sells automated license plate readers to police departments across the United States, and the stolen files show exactly how one device recognizes and logs cars and the people near them. Agencies running Flock hardware should expect these capture rates, retention records, and internal uses to drive local policy fights and open records demands.

sources.title: Hackers Stole Flock's Camera Software, Revealing How the Company Tracks Cars and People
Hackers Got Inside a Flock Camera. Its Data Shows How the System Really Works
Flock camera use by internal affairs unit puts DC police at odds with officers' union

topics.title: KREMLIN Toolkit Force-Installs Browser Extensions
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed KREMLIN on September 16, 2026, a toolkit a banking malware operation has run since mid-2025 that walks past browser installation checks to force malicious Chrome and Edge extensions onto infected machines, where the extensions steal credentials, session tokens, and other sensitive data; Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 published fresh Atomic macOS Stealer activity in which deceptive setup guides talk Mac users into surrendering credentials; and Bruce Schneier flagged a fake CAPTCHA variant that persuades people to download and run the malicious program themselves.
topics.summary: Stolen session tokens survive a password reset and skip the multi-factor prompt, which is why extension-based theft pays. Block unmanaged extension installation through browser policy, revoke sessions after any infostealer detection, and tell staff that a CAPTCHA asking them to paste a command into a terminal is an attack.

sources.title: Malware bypasses browser checks to force install Chrome, Edge extensions
Atomic macOS (AMOS) Stealer Activity
Fake CAPTCHA Scams

business_politics.title: Congress Passes the Russia Sanctions Bill
business_politics.latest_developments: The House passed a sweeping Russia sanctions package Wednesday, September 16, and sent it to President Trump, who is expected to sign it.
business_politics.summary: The bill hands Trump new authority to level tariffs on the largest importers of Russian oil and gas, a group that includes American allies, and it targets Russian officials along with the pillars of Moscow's economy. Lawmakers named the measure for the late Senator Lindsey Graham, and it lands on an energy market already short the barrels that normally move through the Strait of Hormuz.

business_politics.title: The Fed Decides on Rates
business_politics.latest_developments: The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate Wednesday afternoon, September 16, its first increase since 2023 and a unanimous vote, Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation remains "too high," and President Trump answered by calling for borrowing costs of 1% or less.
business_politics.summary: The increase answers August consumer prices running 3.4% and the oil shock from the Gulf war, and new projections show most policymakers expecting one more tightening this year. The Dow industrials fell 500 points and all three major U.S. indexes closed lower for the seventh time in eight sessions, the dollar strengthened, and gold gave back its gains.

business_politics.title: Saudi Arabia Appears to Fire a Chinese Ballistic Missile
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, September 16, that the body of what appeared to be a Dongfeng 15 turned up in the Yemeni desert, the first sign that Saudi Arabia has fired a Chinese ballistic missile, and the Houthis claimed the same day that they shot down a Saudi F-15.
business_politics.summary: The kingdom has absorbed months of Houthi drone and missile attacks on its oil facilities and its Red Sea coast, and the militants now hold the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint. Saudi Arabia reaching into a Chinese missile arsenal widens a war that has shut the Strait of Hormuz to tanker traffic, closed the East-West pipeline, and left Brent near four-month highs.

business_politics.title: Chinese Oil Prices Hit Records
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Wednesday, September 16, that domestic Chinese oil prices reached record highs after the drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and that Beijing has drained enough of its stockpile that it must come back to the world market.
business_politics.summary: China held global crude prices down through the first months of the Iran war by drawing on inventories instead of buying, a cushion analysts told the Financial Times is ending as the country comes off its crash diet. Fresh Chinese buying would land on a market already short the barrels that normally move through the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent near four-month highs and the Hormuz squeeze now pushing Asian buyers to look past long-term liquefied natural gas contracts.

business_politics.title: The AI Slowdown Fight Moves Inside OpenAI and Anthropic
business_politics.latest_developments: OpenAI disclosed a wider set of safety incidents Wednesday, September 16, and adopted new rules for reporting them, saying it hopes competitors follow, a day after the Financial Times reported that staff at OpenAI and Anthropic are struggling over how to turn their chief executives' slowdown rhetoric into practice and the Wall Street Journal reported that dozens of business leaders at a private event pressed President Trump to work with China on joint guardrails.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei's essay against a race to the bottom in model development knocked down memory-chip makers and Nvidia worldwide on Monday, September 14, and Trump called the warnings a hoax. DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg told the Financial Times that AI must not outrun safety controls as his company launched the DeepMind Institute to study artificial general intelligence, and the Journal's markets column argued the buildout slows on its own economics whatever happens on safety.

business_politics.title: Von der Leyen Offers Canada Associate Membership
business_politics.latest_developments: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed Wednesday, September 16, making Canada the first associate member of the European Union, saying the two "see the world with the same eyes."
business_politics.summary: The offer endorses Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's drive to pivot his country toward Europe and away from the United States, and it would create a membership tier that has never existed in the bloc's history. Several EU governments have balked at Carney's parallel call for "middle powers" to line up together against Washington and Beijing, leaving the proposal short of unanimous backing.

around_town.summary: Pennsylvania leads the country in confirmed measles cases this year, with 676 counted on September 11 and four deaths, the most recent reported by the Mifflin County coroner. Allegheny County has stayed clear of the outbreak so far.

sources.title: As Allegheny County prepares for measles cases, director warns of 21 day quarantines

events.summary: The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust and the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series present "Disney's The Lion King" at the Benedum Center in downtown Pittsburgh through Sunday, September 27, the show that opened the Trust's 2026-27 Broadway season.

events.title: Evans City Pumpkinfest, September 19 and 20
events.latest_developments: KDKA previewed Evans City Pumpkinfest on Wednesday, September 16, with Chris Jamison, the Pittsburgh singer who reached the finals of "The Voice," among the performers.
events.summary: Pumpkinfest fills E. Main Street in Evans City, Butler County, on Saturday, September 19, and Sunday, September 20, with food, family activities, and live music.

events.title: The Great Race Comes September 26 and 27
events.latest_developments: KDKA walked through the first steps toward the City of Pittsburgh Great Race on Wednesday, September 16, ten days out from the event.
events.summary: One Great Weekend runs Saturday, September 26, and Sunday, September 27: the Dollar Bank Junior Great Race on Saturday, then the 5K, the 10K, and the One GREAT Challenge on Sunday.

events.title: Luke Bryan's Farm Tour at 1846 Farms
events.latest_developments: KDKA published its guide to the show Tuesday night, September 15, placing Luke Bryan's Farm Tour stop at 1846 Farms in Unity Township, near Latrobe in Westmoreland County, on Thursday, September 17.
events.summary: Bryan has run the Farm Tour for years, playing open fields at working farms, and thousands of fans are expected to fill the Unity Township site Thursday.

sources.title: What to know for Luke Bryan's Farm Tour stop in Westmoreland County

around_teams.title: Porter Practices Limited Again
around_teams.latest_developments: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. took a limited practice again Wednesday, September 16, as the Steelers opened their preparation for the New England Patriots, the Post-Gazette reported.
around_teams.summary: Porter sat out the Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons with his contract unresolved, and sources told the Post-Gazette then that he was healthy enough to play. Head coach McCarthy, who met the media Wednesday before practice, has declined to set any timeline for his return; the Steelers play at New England on Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Joey Porter Jr. is limited again in practice as the Steelers start to prep for the Patriots
Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (September 16) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Freiermuth Reemerges in the Offense
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette wrote Wednesday, September 16, that tight end Pat Freiermuth is working his way back into a central role in Mike McCarthy's offense, and called that a good thing for the Steelers.
around_teams.summary: On SNR Drive the same day, Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler went through the offensive and defensive personnel groupings with The Athletic's Mike DeFabo, who has watched practice this week. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers met the media after Wednesday's session, looking for more from an offense that left plays on the field in the opener.

sources.title: Pat Freiermuth appears to be reemerging in the Steelers offense — and that's a good thing
Mike DeFabo Calls In + We Talk Personnel | SNR Drive (Sept.16) | Pittsburgh Steelers
Aaron Rodgers Press Conference (September 16) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Horwitz Hunts for His Swing
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, September 16, that Pirates first baseman Spencer Horwitz has tried everything to break a season-long slump, searching, in his words, for "the kind of hitter I can be."
around_teams.summary: The Pirates acquired Horwitz to hit in the middle of the order, and the club is playing out the final weeks of a season its playoff hopes have left.

sources.title: Spencer Horwitz is trying everything in search of 'the kind of hitter I can be'

around_teams.title: Benton Wears a Microphone at Practice
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted a full mic'd-up video of defensive tackle Keeanu Benton on Wednesday, September 16, recorded during practice at the team's facility.
around_teams.summary: Benton works the interior of the line alongside Cam Heyward, and the video follows him through drills and position work as the Steelers prepare for the New England Patriots on Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: MIC'D UP: Keeanu Benton (FULL VIDEO) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Watt Walks Through the Pick-Six
around_teams.latest_developments: T.J. Watt joined Not Just Football on Wednesday morning, September 16, to break down his pick-six against the Atlanta Falcons, the snaps he took on both sides of the line, and life as a new father.
around_teams.summary: Cam Heyward and co-host Hayward Heyward run the show; after the Watt interview they went through the Steelers' Week 1 win and the zone-heavy plan the defense used, then looked ahead to the trip to the New England Patriots on Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: T.J. Watt Breaks Down His HUGE Game, New Fatherhood & the Patriots Ahead | Not Just Football

around_teams.title: Dulac Takes Week 2 Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette beat writer Gerry Dulac held his Steelers chat Wednesday, September 16, taking reader questions on the club as it prepares for New England.
around_teams.summary: Dulac has covered the Steelers for the Post-Gazette for decades and runs the weekly chat through the season. The Steelers play at the New England Patriots on Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Gerry Dulac's Steelers chat: 09.16.26

around_teams.title: The Film Says McCarthy's Offense Looked New
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's film study, published Wednesday, September 16, found head coach Mike McCarthy's offense genuinely different in design from what the Steelers ran in recent seasons, with the results still lagging the scheme.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy took over as head coach this year and built the offense around quarterback Aaron Rodgers and receiver DK Metcalf, who drew a poor grade from the paper for the Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers play at the New England Patriots on Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Steelers film study: Mike McCarthy's offense was different but needs better results

team_usa.title: Cavan Sullivan Earns a First U.S. Call-Up
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources told ESPN that Philadelphia Union attacker Cavan Sullivan, 16, will receive his first United States senior call-up for the September and October FIFA international window.
team_usa.summary: Sullivan scored twice and set up another goal in the Union's 5-0 win over San Diego on Sunday, September 13, his first two-goal game in Major League Soccer. He enters a men's pool that turned over after the United States exited the 2026 World Cup, with Real Salt Lake midfielder Diego Luna out for months with a knee injury.

sources.title: Sources: Union's Sullivan, 16, set for first USMNT call-up

team_usa.title: Pulisic Comes Off the Bench in a Milan Loss
team_usa.latest_developments: Christian Pulisic entered as a substitute Wednesday, September 16, as AC Milan opened its Europa League campaign with a 2-0 home loss to Benfica.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the United States captain, has worked back into Ruben Amorim's rotation after missing the start of the Italian season, assisting in a 2-2 draw at Lazio on September 12 in his first appearance since the American exit from the 2026 World Cup.

sources.title: Pulisic subs on as Milan humbled by Benfica in Europa League

team_usa.title: Brazil Ends the U.S. Under-20 World Cup Run
team_usa.latest_developments: Brazil eliminated the United States from the Under-20 Women's World Cup on Wednesday, September 16, winning 5-4 on penalties in the round of 16 after a 1-1 draw through 120 minutes.
team_usa.summary: The exit comes days after Alex Morgan, Crystal Dunn, and Brazil's Marta signed an open letter asking FIFA to align the Under-20 Women's World Cup with the international match calendar, a fight over how national federations release young players for the tournament.

sources.title: U.S. ousted from U20 Women's World Cup in shootout loss to Brazil

team_usa.title: Cole Campbell Commits to the United States
team_usa.latest_developments: Cole Campbell told ESPN on Wednesday, September 16, that he has committed his international future to the United States as he pushes for a first senior call-up.
team_usa.summary: Campbell has been the breakout American of the German season at Elversberg, and his decision adds a forward option to a men's pool that turned over after the United States exited the 2026 World Cup, with Diego Luna out for months with a knee injury.

sources.title: Bundesliga breakout star Campbell committed to U.S., eyes 1st call-up

team_usa.title: Softball's Schiller Draws a Three-Year Ban
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Wednesday, September 16, that American softball player Cam Schiller has accepted a three-year ban for doping with a steroid.
team_usa.summary: The suspension sidelines Schiller through the run-up to softball's return to the Olympic program at the 2028 Los Angeles Games, where the United States will defend a sport it has dominated for decades.

sources.title: U.S. softball player Schiller gets 3-year steroid ban

team_usa.title: Record Ratings for the Women's World Cup Final
team_usa.latest_developments: TNT said Tuesday, September 15, that an average of 1.2 million people watched the United States beat France in the FIBA Women's World Cup gold medal game, a record audience for the event on the network.
team_usa.summary: The United States won 97-79 in Germany on Sunday, September 13, for its fifth straight World Cup title, with Breanna Stewart scoring 22 points and Jackie Young 18 under coach Kara Lawson.

sources.title: TNT says average of 1.2M watched USA in women's FIBA World Cup final

team_usa.title: DeMelo Sues Over Her Cardiac Arrest
team_usa.latest_developments: Racing Louisville FC midfielder Savannah DeMelo sued University of Louisville Health and two physicians, ESPN reported Tuesday, September 15, claiming they failed to diagnose the heart condition that led to her cardiac arrest on the field.
team_usa.summary: DeMelo, a United States international who played in the 2023 Women's World Cup, collapsed during an NWSL match in September 2025. The suit puts a club's medical screening under legal scrutiny at a moment when the league is expanding its player health protocols.

sources.title: DeMelo sues doctors after cardiac arrest during NWSL game

reading.title: Salesforce AI Force, Agents as UI, The Race to Headless
reading.summary: Ben Thompson reads Salesforce's AI Force launch as the company giving up on its user interface as a competitive moat, and argues that is the right call because AI agents are dissolving the interface layer across enterprise software.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands
reading.summary: Zitron argues that the speculative debate over future superintelligence distracts from the concentrated power the current crop of AI companies already holds, and that the people running them have shown what they will do with it.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport, responding to Anthropic employees who said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions, treats superintelligence as a myth while warning that the race toward it inflicts real damage along the way.
